en:
C++

The VEX V5 C++ API Reference explains the classes, objects, constructors, member functions, and variables used in VEXcode V5 C++ projects.

Use this reference when you want to understand how a device or feature is created, check which function signature to use, or compare related member functions in a class.

C++ commands are used in VEXcode V5 C++ projects. C++ API information can also support projects written in Visual Studio Code with the VEX Visual Studio Code Extension.

How to Read a C++ Class Page

A C++ class page usually follows this order:

  1. Introduction - Explains what the class represents and when it is useful.
  2. Derived Classes - Lists any classes that are based on this class, if applicable.
  3. Class Constructor or Constructors - Shows the syntax used to create an object from the class.
  4. Class Destructor - Shows the syntax used to destroy the object and release its resources, if applicable.
  5. Parameters - Explains the constructor parameters used when creating the object.
  6. Example - Shows how to create the object in code.
  7. Member Functions - Lists the functions that belong to the class, often grouped by purpose.
  8. Function Entries - Explains each member function, including available functions, parameters, return values, notes, and examples.

Not every page has every section. For example, some pages do not include derived classes, and some functions do not have parameters or return values.

Common C++ API Elements

Element What it means
Class The C++ type for a device or feature, such as motor or drivetrain.
Object A named instance created from a class, such as motor Motor1 or drivetrain myDrivetrain.
Constructor The code used to create an object from a class.
Member Function A command called on an object, such as myDrivetrain.drive(...).
Available Function One exact function signature that can be used for a member function. Some member functions have more than one available function.
Parameter A value passed into a constructor or function to control what it does.
Return Value A value a function gives back, such as bool, int32_t, or double.

Basic C++ Vocabulary

Term What it means
Variable A name that stores a value, such as int speed = 50;.
Type The kind of data something stores, such as int, double, or bool.
String Text inside quotes, such as "Hello".
int A positive or negative whole number type, such as 90.
double A number type that can include a decimal, such as 25.5.
bool A value that is either true or false.
Argument A value passed into a member function or function call, such as forward in myDrivetrain.drive(forward).

Constructors and Objects

Before using member functions from many C++ classes, an object must exist. The constructor shows how to create that object.

For example, a motor object can be created by giving the constructor the port or configuration information it needs:

motor Motor1 = motor(PORT1, false);

After the object is created, its member functions can be called:

Motor1.spin(forward);

In VEXcode, device configuration is often generated automatically by the Device Menu. In Visual Studio Code with the VEX extension, constructors may need to be written manually.

Choosing the Right Available Function

Some member functions have more than one available function. Each function uses a different set of parameters, so choose the one that matches the values your project needs to provide.

For example, a drivetrain function may have one version that uses the current velocity and another version that lets the project choose a velocity:

void drive(directionType dir);

void drive(directionType dir, double velocity, velocityUnits units);

Both functions call drive, but the second function gives more control because it includes velocity parameters.

Example Function Entry

drive

drive moves the robot forward or reverse forever. The robot will continue to move until it is given another action, like turning or stopping. For RPM or DPS, the limit is changed by the gear ratio of the drivetrain.

Available Functions

void drive(directionType dir);

void drive(directionType dir, double velocity, velocityUnits units);
Parameter Type Description
dir directionType The direction the robot moves: forward or reverse.
velocity double The velocity to drive with from 0% to 100% when using velocityUnits::pct, from 0 to 600 rpm when using rpm, or from 0 to 3600 degrees per second when using dps. If no velocity is provided, the robot drives at the current drive velocity.
units velocityUnits The velocity unit: velocityUnits::pct (percent), rpm (rotations per minute), or dps (degrees per second).

Return Value

This function does not return a value.

Notes

  • drive is non-waiting; the project will continue executing the next line of code immediately after the call.
  • The drivetrain will continue moving until stop is called or another drivetrain movement function is executed.
  • Functions such as isDone and isMoving are not applicable to drive, since it does not use target-based movement.

Example

// Drive forward and back
myDrivetrain.drive(forward);
wait(2, seconds);
myDrivetrain.drive(reverse, 25, rpm);
wait(2, seconds);
myDrivetrain.stop();

Waiting and Non-Waiting Behavior

Some C++ movement functions wait until an action is finished before the project moves to the next line of code. Other functions start an action and allow the next line to run right away.

  • Waiting - The project waits until the function finishes.
  • Non-waiting - The project starts the function and immediately continues to the next line.

Some functions include a parameter such as waitForCompletion to choose this behavior. For those functions, true usually makes the project wait, while false lets the next line run right away.

Commands in Subsections

C++ commands are organized by device or topic. For example, commands for the Drivetrain, Motors, Controller, Brain, Smart Port devices, 3-Wire devices, Console, Logic, and VEXlink are grouped into their own subsections.
zh:
C++ 参考指南

VEX V5 C++ API 参考介绍 VEXcode V5 C++ 项目中使用的类、对象、构造函数、成员函数和变量。

当您想要了解如何创建设备或功能、检查要使用的函数签名或比较类中的相关成员函数时，请使用此参考。

C++ 命令用于 VEXcode V5 C++ 项目。 C++ API 信息还可以支持使用 VEX Visual Studio Code 扩展在 Visual Studio Code 中编写的项目。

如何阅读 C++ 类页面

C++ 类页面通常遵循以下顺序：

  1. 简介- 解释该类代表什么以及何时有用。
  2. 派生类- 列出基于此类的所有类（如果适用）。
  3. 类构造函数或构造函数- 显示用于从类创建对象的语法。
  4. 类解析构造函数- 显示用于销毁对象并释放其资源（如果适用）的语法。
  5. 参数- 解释创建对象时使用的构造函数参数。
  6. 示例- 展示如何在代码中创建对象。
  7. 成员函数- 列出属于该类的函数，通常按用途分组。
  8. 函数条目- 解释每个成员函数，包括可用函数、参数、返回值、注释和示例。

并非每个页面都有每个部分。例如，某些页面不包含派生类，某些函数没有参数或返回值。

常见 C++ API 元素

元素 这意味着什么
级 设备或功能的 C++ 类型，例如motor或drivetrain。
对象 从类创建的命名实例，例如motor Motor1或drivetrain myDrivetrain。
构造函数 用于从类创建对象的代码。
成员函数 对对象调用的命令，例如myDrivetrain.drive(...)。
函数签名 一种可用于成员函数的精确函数签名。一些成员函数有多个可用函数。
参数 传递到构造函数或函数以控制其功能的值。
返回值 函数返回的值，例如bool、int32_t或double。

基本 C++ 词汇

期限 这意味着什么
变量 存储值的名称，例如int speed = 50;。
类型 存储的数据类型，例如int、double或bool。
字符串 引号内的文本，例如"Hello"。
int 正整数或负整数类型，例如90。
双 可以包含小数的数字类型，例如25.5。
布尔型 值为true或false。
参数 传递到成员函数或函数调用中的值，例如myDrivetrain.drive(forward)中的forward。

构造函数和对象

在使用许多 C++ 类的成员函数之前，必须存在一个对象。构造函数显示了如何创建该对象。

例如，可以通过为构造函数提供所需的端口或配置信息来创建电机对象：

motor Motor1 = motor(PORT1, false);

对象创建后，可以调用其成员函数：

Motor1.spin(forward);

在 VEXcode 中，设备配置通常由设备菜单自动生成。在带有 VEX 扩展的 Visual Studio Code 中，构造函数可能需要手动编写。

选择正确的可用功能

一些成员函数有多个可用函数。每个函数都使用一组不同的参数，因此请选择与您的项目需要提供的值相匹配的参数。

例如，传动系统功能可能有一个使用当前速度的版本和另一个让项目选择速度的版本：

void drive(directionType dir);

void drive(directionType dir, double velocity, velocityUnits units);

这两个函数都调用drive，但第二个函数提供更多控制，因为它包含速度参数。

函数输入示例

drive

drive 使机器人持续前进或后退，直到收到转向、停止等其他动作指令。使用 RPM 或 DPS 单位时，速度上限会随传动系统的齿轮传动比而变化。

函数重载

void drive(directionType dir);

void drive(directionType dir, double velocity, velocityUnits units);
参数 类型 说明
dir directionType 机器人移动的方向：forward或reverse。
velocity double 使用velocityUnits::pct时，驱动速度为 0% 到 100%；使用rpm时，驱动速度为 0 到 600 rpm；使用dps时，驱动速度为 0 到 3600 度/秒。如果未提供速度，机器人将以当前驱动速度驱动。
units velocityUnits 速度单位：velocityUnits::pct（百分比）、rpm（每分钟转数）或dps（每秒度数）。

返回值

此函数无返回值。

说明与注意事项

  • drive为非阻塞；项目将在调用后立即继续执行下一行代码。
  • 传动系统将继续运动，直到调用stop或执行另一个传动系统运动函数。
  • isDone和isMoving等功能不适用于drive，因为它不使用目标运动。

示例

// Drive forward and back
myDrivetrain.drive(forward);
wait(2, seconds);
myDrivetrain.drive(reverse, 25, rpm);
wait(2, seconds);
myDrivetrain.stop();

等待和非阻塞行为

某些 C++ 移动函数会等到操作完成后项目才会移动到下一行代码。其他函数启动一个操作并允许下一行立即运行。

  • 等待- 项目等待直到函数完成。
  • 不阻塞- 项目启动该功能并立即继续下一行。

有些函数包含一个参数（例如waitForCompletion）来选择此行为。对于这些函数，true通常会让项目等待，而false让下一行立即运行。

小节中的命令

C++ 命令按设备或主题组织。例如，传动系统、电机、照明、主控器、智能端口设备、3-Wire 设备、Console、Logic 和 VEXlink 的命令被分组到各自的子部分中。
